title.rendered: Top 11 BLDC Ceiling Fans in India (2026)

content.rendered:
A BLDC (brushless direct current) ceiling fan uses a 5-star BEE motor that draws about 28–35 W at full speed, against about 75 W for a standard induction fan — the brands in this guide claim up to 65% less electricity than an unrated fan. That lower draw also means the fan runs noticeably longer on home inverter backup during a power cut. This guide covers 11 BLDC ceiling fans sold in India, from Atomberg, Havells, Crompton, Orient Electric and ACTIVA, and it sticks to what each brand itself publishes: the sweep size, the wattage, the air delivery, the remote and the warranty.

Every fan below links to its Amazon.in listing and to the brand's own website where one exists, so you can check the current variant and details before you buy. Prices change too often to print here, and a star figure tells you little about how a fan will feel in your room, so neither appears in this guide. Where a figure could not be verified, this guide says so instead of guessing.

As an Amazon Associate, we earn from qualifying purchases made through links on this page.

Quick answer

  • Best overall: Atomberg Renesa Enzel — 235 CMM at 35 W, LED speed indicator, Smart IR remote, 2 + 1-year warranty.
  • Highest air delivery: Havells Stealth Air BLDC — 245 CMM at 40 W, RF remote with timer and memory backup.
  • Most modes: Havells FAB BLDC — Boost, Sleep, Breeze and Mop, plus reverse rotation.
  • Longest warranty: Orient Aeon BLDC PRO — 5 years; Crompton Energion Nucleoid — 4 years.
  • Budget picks: Atomberg Efficio Alpha and ACTIVA Gracia, both 28 W class fans with remotes.
  • Large living rooms: Atomberg Renesa+ — 235 CMM at 35 W with Boost mode.
  • Flexible control: Crompton Energion Hyperjet — point-anywhere RF remote with Sleep and Hyper modes.

How to choose a BLDC fan

Sweep size. 1200 mm (48 inch) suits most living rooms and bedrooms in Indian homes; every fan in this guide is 1200 mm. Smaller rooms can use a 900 mm fan and very large halls a 1400 mm one, but those sizes are outside this guide.

Wattage and air delivery. A 5-star BLDC fan draws about 28–35 W at full speed. Air delivery, measured in CMM (cubic metres per minute), is the better comparison between fans than wattage alone — the fans here range from 220 to 245 CMM. Speed in RPM matters less on its own: a fan can spin fast and still move less air than a slower fan with better blades.

Remote type. An IR remote needs a clear line of sight to the fan; an RF remote works from anywhere in the room — the Stealth Air and the Hyperjet use RF remotes, while the Atomberg fans here use Smart IR remotes. Check the remote in the picture before buying: some models in a range share a name but differ in the remote.

Modes. Boost gives a short burst of maximum speed; Sleep lowers the speed through the night; a timer switches the fan off after 2, 4, 6 or 8 hours. Not every fan has all three — the Zeno, for example, has Boost and a timer but no sleep mode, and the plain Stealth Air has a timer but no verified Boost or Sleep mode.

BEE 5-star. Ten of the eleven fans here are BEE 5-star models. The one exception is the Havells FAB BLDC: sibling FAB listings claim 5-star, but the indexed title for the exact ASIN in this guide does not state it, so we do not assert it for that fan.

Warranty. Warranties in this guide run from 2 to 5 years, and they are not all the same thing: the Enzel and Renesa+ give 2 years plus a third year on registration, the Gracia's 5 years applies to this variant only and covers the motor through an authorised service centre, and sibling variants of the same model can carry different warranty periods. Check the warranty line on the listing for the exact variant you buy.

Regulator warning. Remote-controlled BLDC fans must not be run through an ordinary wall regulator: keep the regulator at maximum (or bypass it) and control the fan with the remote. Havells states this plainly for its BLDC range, and running a remote-controlled BLDC fan through a regulator can damage its electronics. This applies to remote-controlled models like the ones in this guide; some BLDC models are sold as regulator-operated variants, which are a different thing.

Check the variant on the listing. ASINs are colour-specific: the Enzel link here is the Gloss Seasand Ivory variant, the Nucleoid link is Gilded Beige, the Aeon PRO link is Cloud Grey, the Gracia link is Sparkle Blue, and so on. Confirm the colour and the variant on the listing page before you buy — the same model name can cover several colours with different ASINs.

BLDC Fan Buying Guide

  • Buy from authorised sellers. Use the brand's own store or its official Amazon storefront, and check that the fan arrives sealed with its remote and warranty card.
  • Check the variant before paying. The same model name can cover several colours with different ASINs: the Enzel link here is Gloss Seasand Ivory, the Nucleoid link is Gilded Beige, the Aeon PRO link is Cloud Grey, the Gracia link is Sparkle Blue, the Renesa+ link is Umber Brown, the Stealth Air link is Pearl White and the Hyperjet link is Opal White — confirm the colour and variant on the listing page.
  • Match the fan to the room. A 1200 mm fan suits most living rooms and bedrooms; for a large hall, pick the highest air delivery in this guide (Stealth Air, 245 CMM, or Renesa+ and Enzel at 235 CMM); for a bedroom, a timer and memory backup matter more than raw airflow.
  • Register for the extra warranty year. The Enzel and the Renesa+ both give a third year on registration — register the fan with Atomberg after buying, or the warranty stays at two years.
  • Keep the regulator at maximum. Remote-controlled BLDC fans are not run through an ordinary wall regulator; keep it at maximum (or bypass it) and use the remote, or the fan's electronics can be damaged.
  • Start with the remote in hand. Check the remote's buttons in the picture: Boost, Sleep, timer and reverse rotation are not on every model, and the remote type (IR or RF) decides whether you must point it at the fan.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which is the best BLDC ceiling fan in India for 2026?
The Atomberg Renesa Enzel is our top overall pick: 235 CMM of air delivery at 35 W, an LED speed indicator, a Smart IR remote and a 2 + 1-year warranty. For the highest air delivery, the Havells Stealth Air gives 245 CMM; for the longest warranty, the Orient Aeon BLDC PRO gives 5 years.

How much electricity does a BLDC ceiling fan save compared to a normal fan?
A standard induction ceiling fan uses about 75 W, while a 5-star BLDC fan uses about 28–35 W. The brands in this guide claim up to 65% less electricity than an unrated fan — that is a manufacturer claim against unrated fans, not a measured guarantee for every home.

Do BLDC ceiling fans work on home inverters?
Yes. Because a BLDC fan draws far less power than a standard fan, it runs noticeably longer on inverter backup during a power cut. Atomberg's Renesa fans are reported to run up to around three times longer on inverter batteries — that multiple is reported for the brand's fans, not a figure we measured.

Can BLDC ceiling fans be controlled with a normal wall regulator?
No — not the remote-controlled models in this guide. Keep the wall regulator at maximum (or bypass it) and control the fan with its remote; running a remote-controlled BLDC fan through an ordinary regulator can damage its electronics. Some BLDC models are sold as regulator-operated variants, which are a different thing and are not covered here.

What is the average lifespan and warranty of BLDC fans?
No brand in this guide publishes a lifespan figure, so none is stated here. Warranties run from 2 to 5 years depending on the model: 2 years for the Efficio Alpha, Epoque, Stealth Air and Hyperjet; 2 + 1 years (third year on registration) for the Enzel and Renesa+; 3 years for the FAB BLDC and the Zeno; 4 years for the Nucleoid; and 5 years for the Aeon BLDC PRO and for this Gracia variant.

Conclusion

Pick by room first and brand second. For most homes, the Atomberg Renesa Enzel is the safe all-round pick; the Havells Stealth Air suits bedrooms and the Atomberg Renesa+ suits large living rooms; the Havells FAB BLDC is the pick if you want the most modes and reverse rotation; the Orient Aeon BLDC PRO is the pick if design and a 5-year warranty matter most; and the Atomberg Efficio Alpha and the ACTIVA Gracia are the budget picks. Every claim in this guide traces back to the brands' own published details or to the linked listings, checked in November 2026 — and where a figure could not be verified, the guide says so.

Researched and checked November 2026. Prices are deliberately not printed in this guide — they change too often — so check the current price on the linked listing before you buy.

title.rendered: Best RO Under ₹15,000 in India 2026: Top Water Purifiers Compared

content.rendered:
Choosing the best RO water purifier under Rs 15,000 is about matching the purifier to your water, not about chasing the highest number on a spec sheet. Indian homes are supplied by borewell, tanker or municipal water, and the right choice depends on your water's TDS, the storage your family needs, and how much water you are willing to waste. This guide covers ten RO purifiers sold in India, from KENT, Aquaguard, Livpure, Kinsco, Pureit and Proven, and it sticks to what each brand itself or its Amazon listing states: the purification stages, the storage, the warranty and the water it suits.

Every purifier below links to its Amazon listing and to the brand's own website, so you can check the current pack, variant and details before you buy. Prices change too often to print here, and a star score tells you little about how a purifier will handle your water, so neither appears in this guide. Check the current price on the linked listing before you buy — and check the exact variant too, because several model names in this guide cover more than one variant.

As an Amazon Associate, we earn from qualifying purchases made through links on this page.

Quick answer

  • Established brand, biggest service network: KENT Grand — 8-litre storage, RO+UF+TDS Control, 1-year warranty.
  • Best water saving: Aquaguard Delight Aquasaver and Aquaguard Marvel NXT, both claiming up to 60% water saving, and Pureit Eco Water Saver, claiming up to 60% recovery.
  • Largest storage: Kinsco Aqua Punch, 15 litres — the only 15-litre tank in this guide.
  • Best for borewell and hard water: Proven Jupiter — 12-litre tank, copper, zinc and alkaline mineralisation, TDS up to 1,500 ppm.
  • Budget pick from an established brand: Livpure Glo Lite — 7 litres, 6-stage RO+UF, 1-year warranty.
  • Compact mineral RO: Pureit Wave Plus — 7 litres, 6-stage RO+UV+Mineral.
  • Watch the water it suits: Aquaguard Sure Delight RO+MC 1X works only with water above 200 ppm TDS.

How to choose an RO purifier

Test your water first. RO is for water with high dissolved solids. As a rough guide, many guides suggest considering RO when TDS rises above 300–500 ppm; below that, a UV+UF purifier is often enough. A handheld TDS meter is cheap, and some purifiers in this guide include one. If your supply is borewell or tanker water, assume high TDS until you have tested it.

Know what each stage does. RO (reverse osmosis) removes dissolved salts and heavy metals. UV kills bacteria and viruses with light. UF and MF are fine filters that polish the water after RO. MC, Mineral Charge and mineral cartridges add calcium and magnesium back after RO has stripped them out. Copper, zinc and alkaline cartridges are mineralisers that brands add for taste and mineral content. A purifier with more stages is not automatically better — what matters is whether the stages match your water.

Match storage to your family. Storage in this guide runs from 6 litres to 15 litres. A small family that uses the purifier through the day can manage on 6–7 litres; a large family, or a home with frequent power cuts, should look at 10 litres and above — the Kinsco Aqua Punch (15 litres) and the Proven Jupiter (12 litres) are the roomiest here.

Ask about water wastage. Ordinary RO purifiers reject a share of the water they take in. Some models in this guide claim up to 60% water saving or recovery — those are brand and listing claims, measured under the brands' own test conditions, so treat them as comparisons between models rather than promises for your home.

Check the warranty and the filter life. Most purifiers in this guide carry a 1-year warranty, with consumables such as filters excluded; filter life is commonly 6,000 litres or up to a year. Check both on the listing, and check whether installation is free and whether a service plan is included.

Check the variant on the listing. The same model name can cover several variants: the Delight name covers the NXT WS, the Aquasaver and the Sure Delight 1X, each with different stages; the Pureit Wave name covers the Plus, Prime and Pro, each with a different stack; and KENT lists a newer 7.5-litre Grand alongside the 8-litre one. Confirm the stages, storage and warranty on the page before you buy.

RO Buying Guide

  • Buy from authorised sellers. Use the brand's own store or its official Amazon storefront, and check that the unit arrives sealed with its warranty card.
  • Check the variant before paying. The same model name can cover several variants: the Delight Aquasaver is RO+UV+UF+MC while the Sure Delight 1X is RO+MC only; the Pureit Wave Plus is RO+UV+Mineral while the Wave Prime is RO+MF; and KENT lists a 7.5-litre Grand alongside the 8-litre one. Confirm the stages, storage and warranty on the listing page.
  • Match the purifier to your water. Borewell and tanker water usually need RO; municipal water with low TDS may not. The Sure Delight 1X in this guide works only with water above 200 ppm TDS — buying it for low-TDS water would be a mistake.
  • Plan for running costs. Filters are consumables and are not covered by the warranty; filter life in this guide is commonly 6,000 litres or up to a year. Check the brand's filter-kit and service terms before buying, since annual upkeep varies by brand, water hardness and how much water you purify.
  • Check installation and service near you. Several listings in this guide include free installation and a first-year service plan. Check that the brand services your pin code before buying, and keep the warranty card and the installer's number.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which is the best RO under Rs 15,000 in India?
There is no single best purifier — it depends on your water. KENT Grand is the established-brand pick with an 8-litre tank; Aquaguard Delight Aquasaver and Marvel NXT are the water-saving picks; Kinsco Aqua Punch has the largest storage at 15 litres; and Proven Jupiter is the pick for borewell and hard water. Match the stages, storage and TDS range to your supply first.

Is an RO purifier necessary for municipal tap water?
Not always. If your tap water TDS is low and the supply is microbiologically treated, a UV+UF purifier may be enough. RO is for high-TDS water — borewell, tanker or hard municipal supply. Test your water's TDS before deciding.

What TDS level requires an RO water purifier?
As a rough guide, RO is usually considered when total dissolved solids rise above 300–500 ppm. Below that, UV+UF purification is often sufficient. Check your own water with a TDS meter rather than guessing from the source alone.

Which RO under Rs 15,000 saves the most water?
On the brands' own claims, the Aquaguard Delight Aquasaver and Marvel NXT both claim up to 60% water saving compared with ordinary RO purifiers, and the Pureit Eco Water Saver claims up to 60% recovery with its Eco Recovery technology. Those figures are measured under the brands' test conditions, so treat them as comparisons between models rather than promises for your home.

What does the warranty usually cover?
Most purifiers in this guide carry a 1-year warranty covering manufacturing defects in electrical parts, with filters and other consumables excluded. The Proven Jupiter listings state 2 years on electrical parts, while Proven's own site states a standard 1-year warranty — check the warranty on the listing at purchase. Several listings also include free installation and a first-year service plan.

Conclusion

Pick by your water first and by brand second. If you want one safe established-brand purifier, KENT Grand will do the job; if you want to cut water wastage, look at the Aquaguard Delight Aquasaver, the Marvel NXT or the Pureit Eco Water Saver; if you need the biggest tank, the Kinsco Aqua Punch holds 15 litres; and if your water is borewell or hard, the Proven Jupiter is built for it. Every claim in this guide traces back to the brands' own published details or their Amazon listings, checked in November 2026 — and every figure the old version of this guide printed for all ten models (the same stages, the same 8 litres, a price, a star score and a comparison score) has been re-checked model by model and corrected where it was wrong.

title.rendered: Top 12 3 Burner Gas Stoves in India (2026)

content.rendered:
A three-burner gas stove is the standard size for most Indian kitchens: enough burners for a pressure cooker, a kadai and a tadka pan at once, without the width of a four-burner. This guide covers twelve stoves from Everflame, BLOWHOT, Glen, Prestige, Vidiem, Surya Flame, Pigeon and Elica, each one checked against its own listing and its maker's site. Every stove here carries its own product photo, checked against the model it illustrates, and every specification comes from a source named in the profile.

A note on prices: this guide lists no prices. Prices on Amazon move daily, and a figure printed here would be stale within days. Use the button under each stove to check the current price on Amazon. As an Amazon Associate, VisitBest earns from qualifying purchases made through links on this page.

Quick answer

Best overall: the Everflame Photon, for its 2 mm stainless-steel body, forged-brass burners and a warranty tied for the longest in this guide. Best auto-ignition option: the BLOWHOT Emerald, the only auto-ignition stove here. Best glass-top option: the Glen Apex. Thickest glass: the Everflame Aurum and the Glen PNG stove, both 8 mm. Best stainless-steel option: the Everflame Prime. Only native-PNG stove: the Glen CT1038GTBBBLCPPN. Only hob-style stove: the Pigeon Twinspark.

How to choose a 3-burner gas stove

Surface first. Stainless steel is the most forgiving surface: it takes knocks, cleans with a scrubber and does not crack. Toughened glass looks better and wipes clean in seconds, but it needs care — no cold water on hot glass, and no dropping heavy vessels on the edges. Glass thickness matters: 8 mm is the thickest here, 6 mm is standard.

Burners second. Brass burners last longer than aluminium ones: they resist warping and corrosion and spread heat evenly. A jumbo burner matters if you cook with large kadais and pressure cookers; a small burner suits simmering and tadka. Burner sizes in millimetres are not printed in this guide because none could be verified for any stove — the layouts are described instead.

Ignition third. Manual ignition needs a lighter or match and never fails. Auto ignition lights the burner when you turn the knob; it comes in three types — piezo, battery and mains — and the battery type needs its cells replaced from time to time. Only one stove here has auto ignition.

Gas type fourth. Most stoves are calibrated for LPG cylinders. PNG needs a larger nozzle because piped gas runs at lower pressure, so conversion must be done by an authorised brand technician — never by a local mechanic drilling out the jets. Only one stove here is built for PNG from the factory.

Then the paperwork. ISI certification is the safety baseline; every stove in this guide that claims it is marked as such. Warranties differ more than the headlines suggest: check whether the years cover the product, the glass, or the burners, because the three are often different. Finally, check the exact variant on the listing before buying — several makers sell a manual and an auto version of the same model under near-identical names.

1. Everflame Photon 3 Burner Gas Stove

The Photon is the stove this guide would put at the top of a shortlist. Its body is jointless stainless steel, 2 mm thick, with three forged-brass PetalArc 5G burners, and it is ISI certified. The ignition is manual, so there is no battery to replace and nothing electronic to fail. It runs on LPG as sold, and Everflame's customer care can arrange a technician visit to convert it to PNG. The warranty is tied for the longest structure in this guide: five years on the body and burners, two years comprehensive, with doorstep service.

Everflame says its stoves carry thermal efficiency of up to 69 per cent; that is the maker's own claim, and no independent test was found, so take it as a claim rather than a measured figure. The body measures 77 by 37 by 10 cm and weighs 9.6 kg. One fact in the listing could not be tied down: whether the front knobs are metal or plastic is not stated anywhere, so the profile does not assert it.

Buying guide

Glass or steel? Steel if the stove will take daily knocks and heavy scrubbing; glass if you want a clean look and a fast wipe-down, and you are willing to treat the top gently. Both are safe when ISI certified and used with pan supports that sit properly.

How many burners do you actually use? Three is the right number for most kitchens. A jumbo burner earns its place if you cook with a large kadai or a 5-litre cooker; if you mostly simmer, the small burner's control matters more than the big one's size.

Auto or manual? Auto ignition is a convenience, not a necessity. It adds a spark mechanism that can fail, and battery types need new cells. Manual ignition is simpler and cheaper to live with. If you choose auto, check which type it is — piezo, battery or mains — before buying.

LPG or PNG? Buy the stove for the gas you have. Converting an LPG stove to PNG needs a larger nozzle fitted by an authorised technician; converting the other way needs the reverse. A stove built for PNG from the factory, like the Glen CT1038 here, avoids the conversion entirely.

Read the warranty twice. A "five-year warranty" can mean five years on the glass and two on the product, or five on the burners and two comprehensive. The table above splits each stove's warranty into its parts; the profiles give the full structure.

Check the variant. The Glen Apex, the Prestige Iris and the Elica Vetro each have a near-identical sibling with a different ignition type or size. The model number in the profile — CT3B70BLBB, 40364, 7031 CT — is the check that matters.

Frequently asked questions

Which is the best 3 burner gas stove in India?

The Everflame Photon is the best overall pick in this guide: a 2 mm jointless stainless-steel body, forged-brass PetalArc 5G burners, ISI certification and a warranty tied for the longest here — five years on the body and burners, two years comprehensive, with doorstep service. If you want a glass top instead, the Glen Apex is the equivalent pick; if you want auto ignition, the BLOWHOT Emerald is the only one here.

Are brass burners better than aluminum alloy burners?

Yes, for Indian cooking. Brass handles high heat better: it resists warping and corrosion over years of heavy use and spreads heat more evenly across the base of the vessel. Aluminium burners are lighter and cheaper, but they warp and corrode sooner. The advantage is durability and even heat, not fuel saving — brass does not preserve fuel efficiency.

Is toughened glass gas stove safe for heavy Indian utensils?

Yes, when the top is ISI certified and 6 mm to 8 mm thick, and the pan supports sit properly so the vessel does not rest on the glass itself. Toughened glass is engineered for pressure cookers and large kadais. Two cautions apply: never pour cold water on a hot glass top, because thermal shock can crack it, and never drop a heavy vessel on the rim or edge, where the glass is most vulnerable. A support plate under the glass, like the one on the Elica Vetro, adds a further margin.

What is the difference between auto ignition and manual ignition?

Auto ignition lights the burner with a built-in spark when you turn the knob, so no matchbox or lighter is needed. It comes in three types: piezo (a crystal that sparks when struck), battery (cells that power the spark and need replacing from time to time) and mains (wired to the power supply). Manual ignition needs a lighter or match for every burner, but there is nothing electronic to fail. Auto ignition is a convenience; manual is simpler and cheaper to live with.

Can 3 burner gas stoves run on both LPG cylinder and PNG pipeline?

Most gas stoves are calibrated for LPG cylinders as sold. To run one on a PNG pipeline, an authorised brand technician must fit a larger nozzle, because piped gas runs at lower pressure than cylinder gas. Never have a local mechanic drill out the jets — the nozzle size is a safety matter, and a drilled jet cannot be un-drilled. Some makers offer the conversion as a paid service. The Glen CT1038GTBBBLCPPN in this guide is built for PNG from the factory, so it needs no conversion at all.

Final verdict

Start with the Everflame Photon for the strongest all-round stove: stainless steel, forged-brass burners and the longest warranty here. Choose the BLOWHOT Emerald for auto-ignition ease, the Glen Apex for a dependable glass top, the Everflame Prime for stainless steel at a lower specification, and the Glen CT1038GTBBBLCPPN if your home runs on piped gas. The Pigeon Twinspark is the pick if you want a hob-style stove, and the Elica Vetro if heavy vessels are the priority.

Three of the stoves in this guide carry flags rather than full verification: the BLOWHOT Emerald, the Vidiem Victor and the Surya Flame Neo Turbo could not be matched to their ASINs in an indexed listing, and the "Neo Turbo" name itself is unverified. They stay in the guide because their photos and their makers are real, but check the model name on the listing before buying any of them.

The site is organised around a few main kinds of coverage, and each kind works a little differently. The sections below describe what a reader will actually find in each part of VisitBest today.

Entertainment and Bigg Boss 20

Our entertainment coverage is currently led by Bigg Boss 20. The season guide connects episodes, contestant profiles and fan polls, and the site also carries a contestants directory, an episode guide, a where-to-watch guide and an explainer on how nominations work. Short visual web stories are added as the season develops, so readers can follow a development in a few screens instead of a long article. This coverage is independent editorial and fan content: as the footer of every page states, VisitBest is not affiliated with the Bigg Boss broadcasters or voting platforms.

Education guides

The education hub collects Top 100 guides to schools, universities and medical institutions in India and abroad. These tables are not all the same kind of list, and each guide says which kind it is. The school guides are directory samples — records drawn from a named directory, such as a board, government or membership directory, under a stated filter — so their numbers are not ranks. The university tables are ordered by a single published research or completions metric, and one medical guide republishes the official NIRF ranking for its first fifty entries, with the remaining entries listed as unranked participants.

Business directory

The business directory holds 700+ public company profiles, organised by category and city, covering sectors such as pharmaceuticals, construction and technology. Each profile carries practical verification notes, and the directory is compiled from public sources — readers are advised to verify details with the organisation before making a commercial decision.

Product and brand guides

Our product and brand guides compare the options in a category — watches, home appliances, ceiling fans, water purifiers and more — with comparison tables that set the brands and models side by side. Product photographs and prices in these guides come from the brands' own Amazon.in listings, and each guide shows the date its prices were checked, because prices change with offers.

How we research, label and update

The byline on our guides is the VisitBest Editorial Team. As the author note on every article puts it, we research public sources, compare practical options, and edit guides for clarity; we update time-sensitive details when reliable information changes, and we flag claims that need verification rather than presenting them as settled.

Photographs matter to how this site works. Our people-list articles use real photographs of the person each profile is about, and credits for the site's Bigg Boss photographs are published on the Image Credits page linked in the footer of every page. Product images come from the brands' Amazon.in listings, as described above.

Polls on VisitBest

Some entertainment pages carry fan polls. Every VisitBest poll is labelled an Open Poll and is run for audience sentiment only: in the site's own words, it is run for entertainment and discussion, it is not official Bigg Boss voting, it does not decide nominations or evictions, and its results are not official vote counts. Official voting for the show, where it is opened, happens only through the official platform announced by the broadcaster.

Advertising and affiliate links

Pages on VisitBest carry advertising, and some product guides contain affiliate links. The disclosure printed on those guides is: "This post contains affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate, we earn from qualifying purchases. This does not affect our editorial independence." Buying through a link may earn the site a commission; it does not change which products a guide includes or how they are compared.

Get in touch

Questions, corrections and suggestions are welcome. The Contact Us page explains what to write to us about, and all messages go to the site's published email address, visitbest10@gmail.com.
